p3_b4.ocr: Fig 4. Enhanced closed-state inactivation of Nav1.5 and Nav1.7 channels by mexiletine and lidocaine. The closed-state inactivation curves were best fitted with two-exponential function. Both mexiletine and lidocaine accelerated the development of closed-state inactivation in Nav1.5 (A) and Nav1.7 (B) channels. The fast (τ1) and slow (τ2) constants of Nav1.5 and Nav1.7 channels are in the same range in control condition. All the τ values and the corresponding fraction in each condition are summarized in Table 4. Note that both mexiletine and lidocaine caused a significant reduction of slow τ2 values in dose-dependent manner, leading to speedy inactivation of either Nav1.5 or Nav1.7. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0128653.g004
